topics.title: Displacement current and the Ampere-Maxwell law

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how a time-varying electric field gives rise to a displacement current i_d = ε0 dΦE/dt that equals the conduction current in a charging capacitor.
State the Ampere-Maxwell law and explain how it restores consistency and symmetry between electric and magnetic laws.
Identify accelerated (oscillating) charges as the source of electromagnetic waves whose frequency equals the frequency of oscillation.
Recall the experimental work of Hertz, J.C. Bose and Marconi on producing and transmitting electromagnetic waves.
Describe the mutually perpendicular orientation of E, B and the direction of propagation in a plane electromagnetic wave.
Use the relations ω = ck, νλ = c and B0 = E0/c to analyse a plane electromagnetic wave.
Relate the speed of electromagnetic waves to μ0, ε0 in vacuum and to μ, ε in a material medium.

topics.title: Electromagnetic spectrum: radio waves, microwaves and infrared

concepts.learning_objective: Explain that regions of the electromagnetic spectrum differ in wavelength or frequency and are classified by production and detection.
Describe the frequency bands, production and uses of radio waves and microwaves.
Explain why infrared waves are called heat waves and their role in the greenhouse effect.

topics.title: Visible light, ultraviolet, X-rays and gamma rays

concepts.learning_objective: Recall the range of visible light and the sources, effects and absorption of ultraviolet radiation.
Describe the production, wavelength ranges and uses of X-rays and gamma rays.
Match each type of electromagnetic wave with its typical production method and detector (Table 8.1).
